incident-bot: High-severity alert: multiple container restarts in serving-pool-3 (gpu nodes). Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOM during prefill, probe: 10 failures in 5m. Pager: Jessica (SRE Oncall) assigned.
Jessica (SRE Oncall): Ack. I'm looking now. Paging Raj for runtime context.
Raj (Runtime): On it. Early tail from logs looks like `CUDA out of memory when allocating 8589934592 bytes` during prefill path. Prefill token batches appear huge — some requests with 60k tokens.
Anna (Infra): Node flapping observed on gpu-node-7 and gpu-node-9. kubelet restarted containers, then crashloop.
Mike (Platform): Noting that autoscaler didn't spin up more pods because admission controller was allowing huge prefill sizes. That's probably the trigger.
Jessica (SRE Oncall): Immediate mitigations: (1) cordon gpu-node-7 to stop scheduling, (2) scale replicas down/up to break OOM loop, (3) apply short-term admission limit to prefill size.
Anna (Infra): Cordon command:```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-node-7
```
Raj (Runtime): I'm pushing a hotfix to runtime-config: set `admission.max_prefill_tokens=8192` and `reject_prefill_over=true` in staging and then prod via canary. Will post diff.
Mike (Platform): Canary deploy to 10% of traffic first. Command:```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/serve-runtime ADMISSION_MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS=8192 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/serve-runtime --selector=canary=true
```
Raj (Runtime): Logs from the failed container (excerpt):```
[2026-01-22 18:14:02] ERROR runtime.prefill: CUDA out of memory. Attempted alloc 8192MB on GPU 0
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/prefill.py", line 142, in handle_prefill
    buffer = torch.empty((...,), device='cuda')
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 8589934592 bytes
```
Jessica (SRE Oncall): Observed impact: ~12% of requests to hosted/model-x with long context are failing (restarts) and hitting 502s for ~10 minutes. Dedicated customers on pool-3 might see degraded throughput. Toya, can you gather a short list of customers who reported errors?
Toya (Customer Success): On it. I already have two support tickets referencing large prompts: acme-inc and quickchat. I'll DM the affected customers and share template.
Raj (Runtime): Canary shows the admit/reject filter working — requests with prefill >8192 tokens are now rejected with a 413-like status and clear message: `prefill too large`. Crash rate for canary pods dropped to zero.
Mike (Platform): Rolling the env var to the rest of prod. Starting:```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/serve-runtime
```
Anna (Infra): After cordoning and draining, gpu-node-7 shows kernel OOM kills in dmesg — potential memory leak triggered by runaway prefill allocations. We'll isolate the node for forensics.
Jessica (SRE Oncall): Next medium-term action items: (A) Add runtime prefill admission as a hard quota per route; (B) Add histogram alert for prefill token distribution; (C) Add backpressure to clients (reject earlier instead of letting runtime allocate). Assigning to Raj/Ana/Mike.
Raj (Runtime): Logged a follow-up: GH issue #2345 with proposed changes: pre-alloc ceiling, streamed prefill parsing to reduce GPU memory spike, and a fallback to CPU-prefill for extreme sizes.
Mike (Platform): Also adding a safety limiter in the API gateway to cap request bytes and tokens so it never reaches the runtime. Patch ready, rolling out after postmortem.
Toya (Customer Success): Message sent to affected customers explaining transient 502s, mitigation (rejected oversized prompts), and ETA for permanent fix. Keeping them updated.
Jessica (SRE Oncall): Final status update: admission control applied cluster-wide, crashloops stopped ~8 minutes after rollout, overall 95% reduction in error rate for the affected model. Node isolation continues for diagnostics. Creating incident ticket and postmortem stub.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED -> mitigated. Severity: Sev2 -> will be revisited if recurrence.
Jessica (SRE Oncall): Postmortem owners: Raj (runtime), Anna (infra), Mike (platform). ETA for complete mitigation (streamed prefill + gateway cap + histogram alerts): 2 weeks.
Raj (Runtime): I'll include a regression test that synthesizes giant prefill requests to avoid regressions.
Mike (Platform): Leaving this thread open for 24h to watch for recurrence. If you see node flaps or OOMs ping here. (:+1:)
Toya (Customer Success): Thanks team. I'll follow up with customers tomorrow with a detailed summary.
